description: We are a father-son team from Taiwan: David (product/design) and Zeyi, age 6, the commander of Moon Base Pals. We are building a cozy 3D-clay browser game teaching kids to run a lunar outpost. Already have character art, story, and prototype. Looking for teammates who love kids games, simple JS/HTML5, 3D/2D art, or video editing. No experience needed — just enthusiasm for space and kids. The whole family is welcome!
summary:
Moon Base Pals is a browser-based mission trainer that lets children as young as six run a Moon base alongside a small robot crew - with no reading required. Across 14 hands-on missions, players clean and aim solar panels, repair dripping water joints, nurse a thirsty space plant, fit and test the wheels of Jade the rover, guide every pal into the storm shelter, and bring Jade safely home. Every mechanic mirrors a real station habit: manage power, keep the water loop closed, grow fresh food, follow maintenance procedure, stay calm in drills, plan before acting.

We built it as a single-file HTML5 game - no install, runs in any browser, fully offline via service-worker cache. Every step is spoken by a local neural child voice (Ana), so pre-readers are never blocked by text. No account, no ads, no data collection. Graduation certificates carry permanent per-player 9-digit numbers.

A real six-year-old playtester completed all 14 missions independently, finishing at the graduation ceremony - his certificate, No. 000000001, was the first ever issued. What we learned: station habits can be taught through pure play to the youngest future astronauts.

details:
What it does and how it works. Moon Base Pals is a browser-based mission trainer for children aged 6-9. Across 14 hands-on missions on a lunar outpost, players care for the base together with a small robot crew: they brush dust off solar panels and aim them at the sun to charge batteries, repair dripping water joints to keep the loop closed, nurse a thirsty space plant back to health, fit, lock and road-test the wheels of Jade the rover, guide every pal into the storm shelter, run a radio handshake with mission control, pack supplies, share power with a beacon, and finally plan the sunny route that brings Jade home. Every mechanic maps to a real station habit: energy management, closed water loops, fresh food, hardware maintenance, safety drills, and planning before acting.

How it is built. A single-file HTML5 game (JavaScript, CSS3, Web Audio API) that runs in any modern browser with no installation, and works fully offline through a service-worker cache. Every instruction is spoken by a bundled local neural child voice (Ana, 388 audio clips), so children who cannot read yet are never blocked by text; WebAudio synthesizes character voices without depending on system TTS. Four robot pals react to the player's choices, progress is saved visually, and the game ends with a graduation ceremony that issues per-player certificates carrying permanent 9-digit numbers - the first, No. 000000001, belongs to our six-year-old commander.

Benefits and intended impact. The project turns the youngest learners from spectators into active mission crew: they practice procedure-following, observation-first problem solving, and calm reactions to drills. It is completely free, has no account, no ads and no data collection, and runs on low-end family hardware - so any family can join a space mission tonight.

Creativity and team factors. We kept the interface 100% picture-and-voice driven after watching our playtester skip anything text-shaped; we set mission difficulty to reward trying ideas rather than punishing mistakes; and we validated everything with a real six-year-old who completed all 14 missions independently, from the first dusty panel to the graduation screen.

Demo. A 29-second video of the real playtester completing four missions is linked in the Project Links section, together with the game itself, the full source repository, and a full 6-minute playthrough.
